$comment: What the car says a few seconds after it links (CarConnectCheck.kt), so the driver
hears up front what will not work this drive instead of finding out by failure.
Inputs: `home` -- the adapter answered /api/status with the paired key (null: the
phone has no Hermes link, so there is nothing to miss); `console` -- the car page
loaded (null: the phone has no console, the car's own screen is the plan);
`grant_missing` -- music goes over the car's media channel and no screen-share grant
is held. Silent (`say: null`) when nothing is wrong. Home down covers the console:
the console is served from home, so naming both would say one fault twice.
One line, the parts joined with a space, in the order of `lines`.

lines.home: I can't reach home, so I can't answer and the car screen is on its own.
lines.console: The console isn't loading, so the car shows its own screen.
lines.music: Music needs the screen-share tap today.

grant missing only

$comment: Written to the car log and posted as one phone notification per car session when home is
unreachable at the connect check (the owner, 2026-11-08: the WireGuard app showed the phone
connected and the car linked, yet AURA could not reach home). Android keeps an app inside a
VPN off the car's Wi-Fi, so AURA has to be excluded from a VPN app and carry its own tunnel.
Null when home answers, when the phone has no Hermes link, or when AURA runs its own tunnel.
`{vpn}` is the VPN apps found on the phone joined with ' or ', else `vpn_fallback`. `{name}` is the worn
pack's name and `{app}` the app's fixed label; the cases are said in `worn`, the default pack, so both are it.
remedy.title: {name} can't reach home from the car
remedy.text: In the car Android keeps an app inside a VPN off the car's Wi-Fi, and an app left outside it has no way home. Give {name} its own tunnel: {name} > Settings > WireGuard > Scan WireGuard QR, with a peer of its own (one peer can't be up twice). Then exclude {app} in {vpn}.

cases.name: home down, no tunnel, WireGuard installed
cases.remedy: In the car Android keeps an app inside a VPN off the car's Wi-Fi, and an app left outside it has no way home. Give AURA its own tunnel: AURA > Settings > WireGuard > Scan WireGuard QR, with a peer of its own (one peer can't be up twice). Then exclude AURA in WireGuard.

cases.name: home down, no tunnel, no VPN app found
cases.remedy: In the car Android keeps an app inside a VPN off the car's Wi-Fi, and an app left outside it has no way home. Give AURA its own tunnel: AURA > Settings > WireGuard > Scan WireGuard QR, with a peer of its own (one peer can't be up twice). Then exclude AURA in your VPN app.
